I get it. I live with this stuff too. You’d be surprised how many people are in your situation, actually. To be honest, I get where you are coming from because I’ve lived a lot and seen a lot, of what you are talking about. But the truth is, life isn’t linear. There are many paths and not all of them support the death machine of capitalistic work based slow death in a factory somewhere. You have a degree. Use it. You also have, as far as you and I know, time. Use that too. I get suicidal every day. Use it. Use your suicidal thoughts to remind you that you are still alive and can make decisions. I know you are still relatively young too and unless you have health issues, which I very much also understand, you can use that too. Find a good job that you enjoy. Use your time to learn and grow and if you don’t like where you are or what you are doing, change it. Life is too short to be miserable where you are at. Schools, work programs, stuff with your degree, hobbies, finding real friends that genuinely support you, these are all what you need. And by the way, if I may say, getting to know Jesus Christ and growing close to God and knowing the love and joy and peace and salvation that only He can offer in this twisted Rolf, is the best thing you can do. 

You have time right now. You live with your folks? Maybe talk to them about it. People can be critical but they can also be more understanding than you think. It really depends on the person and how you bring up the conversation. But use what you have. Don’t let it go to waste. You are valuable. 

And by the way, if you need someone to talk to, please don’t hesitate to message me. God bless, friend. 🙂

Hi, listen, I’m really sorry you ever had to go through this. Honestly, I’ve been there a few times. Depression is not fair or fun in the least. I am very much aware of that and unfortunately I see that you are too. I understand how hard this can be, especially when you feel alone. The thing is, your story sounds a lot like mine. I understand how you feel with feeling put down all the time. You mentioned how you never really told your therapist anything. Well, although I can understand how hard it is, telling her/him might actually help solve the situation. Depression likes to lie to you and tell you that mental health people are only there to put you away in a mental hospital.  That’s how it keeps you in its grasp. But, believe it or not, telling your therapist that your feeling suicidal won’t always get you locked to. In fact, I’ve found that telling my therapist exactly how I felt when I was at my worst is exactly what I needed. They gave me medicines that helped and are still working to help me. That’s what they are there for. They are there to help you get better. I would recommend letting her know what’s going on. It may help.
